participants: DOE Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response
new_pending_items.summary: Sandia describes repeatable cyber-physical test environments for grid AI and reports an existing proof-of-concept evaluating an AI-enabled industrial-control intrusion detector. STAISYS combines emulation, threat modeling and statistical testing across operating configurations.
new_pending_items.what_changed: Provides implementation and proof-of-concept details beyond the earlier AI-FORTS funding announcement; DOE's November 16 follow-up highlights the grid-resilience use case.
new_pending_items.significance: Tests AI as part of an operational energy system, helping identify vulnerabilities and readiness limits before deployment. No quantitative security-performance gain is established in these reports.

published_items.title: INL launches Arco GPU supercomputer to support Genesis nuclear research
published_items.date_basis: Actual first repository addition; America/New_York. Source publication date retained separately.
published_items.source_date_note: November 18 announcement newly verified and added November 27; not a new November 27 launch.
published_items.project: Arco / Idaho National Laboratory Computing Facility / Prometheus
published_items.summary: INL deployed the NVIDIA H200-based Arco system alongside Teton and gained a DOE Office of Nuclear Energy user-facility designation. The computing resources support Genesis Mission work, including the Prometheus nuclear-energy collaboration.
published_items.what_changed: Arco adds GPU capacity for nuclear modeling, simulation and AI research; INLCF's designation expands access for external researchers.
published_items.significance: Adds computing infrastructure for nuclear AI workflows and a user-facility access route. This is an infrastructure announcement, not proof of achieved reactor-development speedups.
published_items.affiliation_evidence: DOE explicitly identifies Arco and Teton as supporting Genesis and Prometheus. INL's Prometheus documentation independently identifies the project as Genesis Phase II.
published_items.deduplication_note: No Arco article exists in the 62-item archive or current review queue. DOE's November 18 companion repeats the same launch, facility designation, core specifications and quotations; retained as corroboration. Existing broad Prometheus mentions do not replace this infrastructure announcement.
